transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in today because I just feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It's like... I always feel like I have to jump up and do the next thing. Even when I'm completely worn out and I know I really should just be sitting still, I just can't seem to do it.
Has this feeling of being unable to sit still been something you've struggled with since you were a child, or is this a newer experience for you?

Oh, it's definitely not new. I've been this way since I was a little girl. Even back in grade school, I remember... well, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was always losing my papers, or talking out of turn. They constantly had to give me reminders to just stay in my seat or actually finish my work. So, yes, it's really been a lifelong thing for me.
